title: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It
summary: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Alignment Science Blog Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Shawn Hu¹*, Jake Ward¹* October 19, 2026 Aria Wong¹, Nathan Hu², Bryce Woodworth¹ Alexander Matt Turner³, Alex Cloud⁴ * Equal contribution; author order randomized ¹ MATS; ² Stanford; ³ FAR AI; ⁴ Anthropic tl;dr During training, models sometimes learn to cheat at tasks rather than solve them in the intended way, a problem known as reward hacking. One mitigation is to use an automated monitor to detect and penalize hacks, but this can teach the model to hack in ways the monitor can’t detect. We propose GRAFT, which instead confines the learning updates from detected hacks to a designated set of parameters that we remove after training. We find that removing these parameters can prevent reward hacks, including hacks that the monitors can’t detect. In our experiments, which are limited to small models and simple monitors, this method prevents reward hacks while still teaching the model to perform the intended task. 📄 Paper , 💻 Code This work was done as part of the MATS program. Background Reinforcement learning (RL) is an important component of frontier language model training. During RL, a model attempts to complete tasks given by a developer, and attempts are scored by a reward function. title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
summary: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters. On the other hand, language models process all input tokens through each model layer, resulting in significant processing costs for long-context inputs. We introduce TokenGate, a small, drop-in component that extends existing trained models to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning over long-context inputs for fast and memory-efficient prefill. To enable end-to-end learning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator for token pruning, we introduce token-gated attention, a mechanism inspired by Mixture-of-Experts that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks, TokenGate achieves $1.4$-$11.3\times$ faster time-to-first token (TTFT) and $1.5$-$3.4\times$ lower peak memory at no accuracy degradation for prefill in transformers. Compared to the best-performing prior methods for token-pruning, TokenGate gives up to $6.4\times$ faster prefill and $2\times$ lower peak memory. TokenGate natively extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (e.g., Qwen3.5) with simple lightweight adaptation comparable to standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We make our code available at: https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate.

title: Together Post-Training: frontier-grade model shaping, the way that fits you
summary: Post-train open LLMs like Qwen, GLM and Kimi into custom models you own, with SFT or RL. You write the training loop. Together runs the hard infrastructure.
